story_type: historic bomber launch from a carrier in heavy seas, deck crashes
hook: 16 bombers, a pitching carrier deck, and no way back
narration: Sixteen Army bombers had to take off from a Navy carrier in the open Pacific.
It was April eighteenth, nineteen forty two, and the target was Japan.
At seven thirty eight that morning, a Japanese patrol boat spotted the ships.
The Hornet was still about six hundred fifty nautical miles from Japan, so the bombers had to launch early.
Carriers steam into the wind for a launch, so air is already rushing over the deck before a plane starts rolling.
The lead bomber had just four hundred sixty seven feet to get airborne.
And the flight deck pitched and rolled in the Pacific swells.
The same Navy film shows what a moving deck could do. A fighter nosed over on landing.
A dive bomber crashed into the catwalk, and the crew came running.
[short pause] Every man in those bombers knew it was a one-way trip.
outcome: All sixteen bombers were safely airborne by nine twenty that morning.
title: B-25s off a pitching carrier deck, 1942
description:
Navy film from April 1942 shows Army B-25 bombers launching from USS Hornet in rough Pacific seas for the Doolittle Raid on Japan, and carrier planes crashing on landing.

Footage: U.S. Navy film (Navy Photographic Center, National Archives 428-NPC-895), Naval History and Heritage Command, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/516425/doolittle-raid-b-25s-launched-tokyo-raid
